correctness.rationale: Relative ranks of iid continuous labels are uniform. A maximal run of ℓ selected positions uses ℓ+1 labels; two distinct runs use disjoint labels because at least one position is unselected between them. This factors the normalized signed moment as a product of A_{ℓ+1}(−1)/(ℓ+1)!, including the trivial moment at the empty mask. The classical Eulerian exponential generating function at −1 is 1+tanh z, giving zero for positive even degrees and the indicated nonzero signed tangent numbers for odd degrees. The admissible masks are uniquely tiled by 0 and 11, so their count at length m is F_{m+1}, starting with one word at m=0 and m=1. At m=n−1 the real Walsh basis diagonalizes the operator, with the claimed rank and nullity, including n=2. Every singular value is the absolute value of a multiplier, at most the total kernel mass n!, attained at the trivial character. Binet gives the stated fraction. The supplied verifier, inspected but not run, is an exact bounded consistency check, not the proof.
residual_risks: Uniform adjacent ordinary descents only, with unnormalized convolution; no condition-number conclusion for the nonzero subspace.

evidence: BDF's correlation for a set with blocks of lengths a_j is ∏_j 1/(a_j+1)!. Expanding the comparison product assigns each selected block of size ℓ a weight (−2z)^ℓ/(ℓ+1)! in the length generating function for one run's signed moments. If U is the sum of those weights for ℓ≥1, the signed moments have series (1+U)/(1−z(1+U))=tanh(z)/z, by cutting at the first unselected bit. This gives exactly the local signed factors; separated mask runs factor by the same BDF correlations. The Coxeter formula yields the same product directly.
